outline.description: This chapter introduces the concept of context windows in Large Language Models (LLMs), why they are limited, and the challenges associated with extending them to handle millions of tokens.
subtopics: Definition of the Context Window
The impact of context window size on LLM performance
Challenges in extension: Catastrophic values and out-of-distribution issues
The scarcity and cost of long-form training data
The trade-off between long-context extension and short-context performance

outline.description: Before diving into extension methods, this chapter provides the necessary mathematical background on RoPE, the standard positional encoding used by models like LLaMA and Mistral.
subtopics: The need for positional information in Transformers
Mechanism of Rotary Positional Embeddings (RoPE)
Understanding rotation frequencies and angles
The role of the base value (e.g., 10,000) in RoPE
RoPE in the context of the attention mechanism

outline.description: This chapter reviews the current state-of-the-art methods for extending context windows and explains their limitations, providing the motivation for LongRoPE.
subtopics: Linear Position Interpolation (PI)
NTK-aware Interpolation and Extrapolation
YaRN (Yet Another RoPE extensioN) and frequency-based grouping
Comparative analysis: Linear vs. Non-linear interpolation
The 'crowded positions' problem in high-ratio interpolation

outline.chapter_title: The Theory of Non-Uniformity in Interpolation
outline.description: This chapter explains the core discovery of the LongRoPE paper: that positional interpolation should not be uniform across dimensions or token positions.
subtopics: Non-uniformity across RoPE dimensions: High vs. Low frequency
Non-uniformity across token positions: The importance of initial tokens
Empirical evidence for non-uniformity in LLaMA2
Information entropy in positional embeddings
Hypothesizing the optimal rescale factors

outline.chapter_title: Evolutionary Search for Optimal RoPE Factors
outline.description: This chapter details the algorithmic approach used to find the best rescale factors for RoPE without relying on human-designed rules.
subtopics: Problem formulation: Minimizing perplexity via search
Defining the search space: Rescale factors (λ) and position thresholds (n)
The Evolutionary Search Algorithm: Mutation and Crossover
Optimization techniques: Optimized initial population and Monotonically non-decreasing constraints
Evaluating candidates using perplexity on sample datasets

outline.description: This chapter describes the practical pipeline for extending a model's context window to 2 million tokens using a multi-stage approach.
subtopics: The limitations of direct fine-tuning at extreme lengths
Stage 1: Search and fine-tuning for medium extension (up to 256k)
Stage 2: Second positional interpolation for extreme extension (up to 2048k)
Integrating fine-tuning with non-fine-tuning extensions
Analysis of the 8x extension capability without fine-tuning

outline.description: Extending the window often breaks the model's ability to handle short sequences. This chapter explains how LongRoPE recovers this performance.
subtopics: The 'crowding' effect on original context windows
The strategy for shorter context window recovery
Searching for specialized factors for 4k and 8k lengths
Dynamic adjustment of RoPE factors during inference
Comparing recovered performance against original baselines

outline.description: This chapter explains how to rigorously test long-context LLMs and analyzes the results achieved by LongRoPE.
subtopics: Metrics for long-context evaluation: Perplexity vs. Task Accuracy
The Passkey Retrieval task: Measuring 'Needle in a Haystack' capabilities
Evaluating on standard benchmarks (MMLU, HellaSwag, etc.)
Ablation studies: Analyzing the contribution of dimension and position non-uniformities
Comparative performance: LongRoPE vs. PI, NTK, and YaRN
